(a) the closed timelikes present in the asymptotically flat region of this space– time make the Hawking radiation unclear to study and (b) the Smarr formula for this black hole, derived recently, can be verified via the semi-classical approach.

the quantum field theoreticity of the rotating Gödel spacetime and its implications for the Hawking radiation and the Smarr formula.

the rotating Gödel metric is an interesting and useful space–time for studying the quantum aspects of the black hole physics.
a semi-classical study of particle emissions from the rotating Gödel space–time, as a black hole, is possible and is a viable alternative to the quantum field theoreticity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Gödel black hole has an interesting structure, but it is not a good black hole for studying quantum field theoretic effects.

the semiclassical approach, which is the only approach available at present for the Gödel black hole, is consistent with the Smarr formula for the rotating Göodel black hole, and is a viable alternative to the quantum field theoretically study of Hawking radiation in this space–time.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the closed timelikes present in the asymptotics of the rotating Gödel space–time, and the fact that a large part of the space–time is inaccessible to geodesics, makes the study of the Hawing radiation in this background a difficult task, which we leave open for future investigations.
